note: The whole quarter and the confirmed FY guide went out by ad-hoc on 12 Nov at 13:17 CET and traded for four hours before the window opened, so the 13 Nov detail report carries only an unseen operating cash-flow line on a thin name: a pre-released period with an unchanged guide is a near-zero at p_up ~50.

Veidekke's 12 Nov Q3, with margin improvement 'particularly strong in Norway, in both building and infrastructure' and 12-month executable orders +14%, is a dated primary read-through to AFG's Norwegian segments that AFG's flat 12 Nov close did not take, on a name that beat four quarters running and was paid for three of them; the period is not pre-released, so abs_move sits above the 2.06% observed median, which mixes annual reports and presentation notices with real results days (-9.0% to +6.5%).

Hasbro's Magic +34% to $616m in the identical calendar quarter plus two in-quarter Pokemon releases point to a strong partner-TCG sell-in, but the bar moved up against it (Modular Finance 11-contributor consensus of 10 Nov at EUR 490m / 97.4m sits above SB1's own bullish 7 Oct preview), so a genuinely new quarter with a high public bar gets a full 7% move scale and only a modest directional lean.

The main line is pre-released: the FY guide was raised for the third time on 8 Oct and the stock rerated ~8% on it, so the only unpriced items are a likely new buyback tranche (positive) against the first 2027 Public Preparedness framing from a CEO five weeks in office, on a stock 7% off its high with a +25% 60-day run-up (negative); the two roughly cancel.

Q3 EBT and the raised guide were pre-released by ad-hoc on 5 Nov, leaving operating cash flow as the one new line with sign risk (H1 OCF -EUR 101.7m, Q2 -EUR 112.5m against +EUR 45.2m, with business volume now +19% and memory-driven inventory), and this name has sold every report day following an ad-hoc raise (-3.78%, -9.52%, -3.71%, -1.99%).

Two live forces that nearly cancel: the CFO already pre-guided Q3 down (so the quarter is worth 0) and the 30 Sep working capital behind a 12% non-pre-emptive placement will be ugly, but a company three weeks from a bookbuild has every incentive to publish hard Q4 order and price numbers, and the stock is at a 60-day low after -7% on the placement; I file the Polish September output figure the hunter dropped, because management commentary about rising orders is not a primary document contradicting a production statistic.

H1 ran +9.1% revenue and +37.6% EBIT against a guide of 'around 5%' growth that was only confirmed, and Q3 2025 is a soft comp (group +1.4%, medical held back by the Cynosure supply interruption), so a firmed or raised FY guide is live on a four-analyst, EUR 0.6m-a-day name where day-after reactions have run +7.25% and +2.82%; InMode's flat Q3 is a weak offsetting proxy.

Both findings are public macro series the sell side already models and they point opposite ways (Terna national wind -20.3% and -24.2% in July and August against PUN prices far above 2025 on a hedged book), so the residual is only a mild negative from volume plus the risk of the 520-590m guide narrowing low after 295m in H1, on a utility whose prints move ~1-1.5%.

Alantra's 23 Sep note reports management expecting a strong Q4 'supported partly by orders that slipped out of Q3' — a company-sourced statement that the quarter about to print is soft — and 30 Sep net debt is likely above June's EUR 7.2m on the component inventory build Emera's October commitment itself cites, while the stock has already run +12.3% in five sessions on the EUR 1.17 reserved raise to EUR 1.30; the insider subscription is a real positive but it is also the cause of the run-up.

The two load-bearing findings genuinely offset: management flagged the 20.9% Q1 margin as not a run-rate with marketing and S/4HANA costs falling in Q2-Q3 against a hard EUR 4.9m / 22% Q2 comp, while the headline H1 will show revenue up 12-17% and recurring revenue still building; the EUR 42k-a-day buyback is a quarter of median turnover and dampens a downside gap, so this is a wide-move, no-direction name.

Tying the company's own 9M consensus (nat cat 5.1% of premiums) back to the CFO's guided ~EUR 300m July and a plausible EUR 150-300m share of the EUR 3.3bn Raphaela industry loss implies the consensus cat line is too heavy, which is a small P&C beat; against it sit the Barclays mark-to-market and Solvency risk and the fact that this is a 15-analyst mega-cap that publishes its own consensus and whose prints move 1-2%.

Bucher's derived Q3 (orders +7.8%, sales +6.4%) and Parker's +9.4% North American organic growth with accelerating orders both point to organic acceleration against easy comps, but all of it is public and partly inside a +9.65% 20-day run-up with no company news, and the release lands in session around 15:00 CET so only about 2.5 hours of the reaction falls inside the scored window — which is what caps abs_move, not my uncertainty.

The day after a -72% capitulation on 30% of shares outstanding the move is going to be enormous whatever the direction (20-day realised vol 261%), and the two sourced items point opposite ways: Q3 cash of about SEK 85m against an SEK 89m market cap is a floor, while a shortened runway or going-concern wording is live because the 'into Q4 2027' claim assumed an overallotment that was not taken; large size, almost no directional view.

The H1 operating story was pre-released inside the 1 Oct placing RNS (lettings ahead of ERV, valuation broadly stable, LFL NRI 3-5%, FY27 EPS flat), so that finding is worth 0; what is left is a possible guidance nudge against a 10-year gilt at 5.26% on a 17-analyst stock already 16% off its low and at the consensus target — and the last time this company raised LFL guidance at H1 the shares fell 5.26%.

The best-evidenced call of the day: Italian diesel ran about +29% y/y through Q3 (Jul +20.6, Aug +28.2, Sep +37.3) against roughly +26% in Q2, the quarter whose EBITDA fell 16% on fuel and energy by the company's own attribution, while the only visible bar (Intesa, 5 Aug) still has H2 EBITDA slightly UP and was set before September and October printed; six analysts, no note since August, no Q3 preview, and every 2026 print has missed on margin and fallen. Sized down only because the release lands mid-afternoon and the history shows most of the move arriving the next session, outside the window.

CoreWeave (8.6% of rents, about 80% of the data-centre MW) raised FY guidance on 10 Nov and rose 24.7% on 11 Nov while MRL moved +0.6% and gave it back, so one of the two pillars of the October de-rating eased without being marked, and the 9M call is the first chance to restate tenant exposure; held to a modest size because it is still a counterparty proxy on a 21-analyst name that sold its last guide raise.

A takeover stub: the EUR 81 cash offer closed at 94.04% with a squeeze-out planned, spot is EUR 78.80 and 20-day realised vol is 9.7%, so the quarterly statement cannot move the floor and the only asymmetry is a possible regulatory or closing update narrowing the 2.8% spread.

The headline 9M profit is mechanical and pre-announced (the EUR 54m+ Bending Spoons gain realised 1 July) and a holding trades on NAV and discount, so that finding is worth 0; the buyback at 13.27% of capital is a known bid and Bending Spoons' own print lands on 20 Nov, outside the window, leaving essentially nothing.

The >EUR 6.5bn sales guide needs about EUR 3.44bn in H2, +16% on H1, after Q2 sales grew only 2.9%, and Renta 4's published model already sits 5% below it, while the stock has run +20% in 20 sessions and +7% in five to its highest since the Middle East disruption began — a guidance trim or softening into that is the day's second-clearest asymmetry, partly offset by the ruled-out provisions, the 30% payout dividend and record intake, all of which are public.
